title: Autonomous Field Rover & Sensor Platform
summary: A modular Raspberry Pi/Linux field robotics platform for geotagged sensing, remote diagnostics, computer-vision development, and future autonomous operation.
overview: I am developing a modular field robotics platform for sensor integration, field-data collection, computer-vision development, and future autonomous operation. The current prototype is intentionally human-powered so the sensing, electrical, software, and safety systems can be validated before powered mobility is introduced.

The platform is designed as a reusable robotics system rather than around one demo. Current work emphasizes reliable field data, repeatable diagnostics, and architecture that can migrate to a larger powered rover.
objectives: Integrate the primary perception and localization sensors.
Build a repeatable image and sensor-data pipeline.
Develop remote monitoring, health checks, and diagnostics.
Create a modular electrical and CAN communications architecture.
Establish safety-state logic before powered mobility.
Preserve raw field data for future computer-vision development.
process: Separated high-bandwidth sensing from embedded control and designed around Raspberry Pi/Linux high-level compute with CAN-based expansion.
Built repeatable image-capture services with stable USB device mapping, remote access, health monitoring, and diagnostics.
Developed safety-state logic and system-health reporting before powered mobility.
Structured capture around reusable imagery, diagnostics, timing, and location information.
results: Raspberry Pi/Linux onboard computing and remote access are operational.
Camera capture, stable device mapping, and health monitoring are operational.
Core safety-state logic and structured data-capture infrastructure are implemented.
Sensor integration and localization testing are continuing before powered mobility is added.
evidence: Show sensing, compute, communications, safety, and logging together.
Establish the physical system and current prototype state.
Prove remote observability and repeatable capture tooling.

title: UBCO Aerospace — 2026 Urban Firefighting Drone System
summary: Electrical-system leadership for a multi-drone autonomous firefighting project that placed 6th overall and won the 2026 AEAC Innovation Award.
overview: From September 2024 to June 2026, I served as Director of Electrical for the UBCO Aerospace Team. The 2026 project centered on an urban-firefighting mission requiring multiple unmanned aircraft to perform scouting, navigation, sensing, target detection, and coordinated operation.
My role combined electrical architecture, power electronics, sensor integration, design reviews, work breakdown, and cross-disciplinary integration with software, autonomy, and mechanical teams.
objectives: Provide reliable power to flight computers and sensors.
Integrate navigation and perception hardware.
Support autonomous takeoff/landing, scouting, localization, and vision tasks.
Reduce electrical-system weight while improving fault containment.
Coordinate interfaces between electrical, mechanical, autonomy, and software systems.
role: Custom power-converter and power-distribution PCB design
LiDAR, RTK GPS, IMU, camera, LTE, and CAN integration
process: Introduced milestones, work-breakdown structures, peer review, and component/system roadmaps.
Integrated 2D LiDAR, RTK GPS, IMU, stereoscopic/Ethernet cameras, LTE, and CAN bus.
Designed a 50 V to 5 V, 40 W synchronous converter with filtering and protection.
Designed a protected distribution PCB with resettable electronic fuses and inrush-current limiting.
results: Placed 6th overall at the 2026 AEAC competition.
Won the 2026 AEAC Innovation Award.
Completed a custom 50 V-to-5 V converter at approximately 92% efficiency.
Built a multidisciplinary integration process connecting electrical design to autonomy, sensing, communications, and mechanical constraints.
evidence: Anchor the page in the completed system and result.
Show a major individual hardware contribution.
Explain sensor, compute, power, and communications integration.

title: Mountain Resort Data Collection System — UBC Capstone
summary: A low-power distributed sensing system using ESP32 edge nodes, LoRa networking, ToF/mmWave sensing, custom power electronics, and a Linux gateway.
overview: My UBC capstone team developed a distributed data-collection system intended for harsh mountain-resort deployment. Edge sensing nodes communicated over LoRa to a Linux gateway, spanning power electronics, sensing, wireless networking, enclosure constraints, and system-level validation.
objectives: Develop low-power remote sensing nodes.
Provide reliable long-range wireless communication.
Design custom node power electronics and protection.
Demonstrate end-to-end data flow from sensors to dashboard.
process: Used ESP32 edge nodes with LoRa, ToF/mmWave sensing, and a Linux gateway.
Designed node power conversion, battery monitoring, and low-voltage shutoff.
Researched batteries, enclosure requirements, energy needs, and ISED 915 MHz constraints.
Bench-tested electronics and demonstrated outdoor communication and sensing-to-dashboard flow.
results: Demonstrated more than 500 m outdoor LoRa communication.
Demonstrated end-to-end sensing-to-dashboard data flow.
Completed custom PCB schematic, layout, assembly, and bench testing.
evidence: Show node → LoRa → gateway → dashboard flow.

title: “Chimera” FPV Drone Frame
summary: A crash-driven custom FPV frame redesign focused on center-of-mass placement, crash behavior, packaging, and lightweight manufacture.
overview: After an FPV crash broke an arm on an existing frame, I redesigned the aircraft around improved component packaging, center-of-mass placement, crash behavior, and a smaller footprint.
objectives: Improve mass distribution and packaging.
Reduce weight and footprint.
Create intentional mechanical failure points.
Prototype cheaply before final manufacture.
process: Used the previous crash to identify weaknesses and redefine priorities.
Moved the battery and electronics and refined geometry around mass and packaging.
3D printed successive designs and checked fit and behavior.
Produced final components from carbon fiber and aluminum.
results: Completed the final frame in 2024.
Continued flight/crash testing informed future modification ideas.
evidence: Show final geometry and component packaging.

title: Custom 5-inch & 3-inch FPV Drones
summary: Two custom FPV aircraft built from individual components, including a sub-250 g 3-inch platform and a 5-inch aircraft documented at 90+ km/h.
overview: I built two custom FPV multirotors from individual components rather than preassembled systems. Both platforms required component selection, wiring, soldering, protocol research, FPV video integration, troubleshooting, and flight testing.
objectives: Build complete FPV aircraft from discrete components.
Develop electrical integration and troubleshooting skills.
Meet a sub-250 g constraint on the smaller aircraft.
process: Integrated propulsion, flight controller, receiver, camera/video, and wiring hardware.
Used specifications and wiring diagrams, soldered connections, and checked for faults.
Used repeated real flights and simulator practice.
results: The larger aircraft was documented at 90+ km/h cruising speed.
The smaller aircraft was completed around a sub-250 g constraint.
evidence: Prove the aircraft operate in real flight.

title: Axial Flux Brushless DC Motor
summary: A custom axial-flux BLDC motor and geared scissor mechanism built with custom coils, 3D-printed structure, and iterative troubleshooting.
overview: This university project developed a custom axial-flux BLDC motor and geared scissor-cutting mechanism using 3D-printed mechanical parts, custom-wound coils, and existing drone hardware.
objectives: Create a functional custom BLDC motor.
Balance magnetic performance, air gap, rigidity, and manufacturability.
Demonstrate the motor under mechanical load.
process: Designed six coils in wye configuration while managing air gap and rigidity.
3D printed the structure and assembled the motor.
Identified PLA thermal deformation and rotor stability as V1 limits.
results: Successfully ran the motor and drove the scissor mechanism.
Received a documented project grade of 100%.
evidence: Show the motor doing mechanical work.
Turn the V1 limitation into an iteration story.

title: Custom Upgraded 3D Printer
summary: A heavily modified Ender 3 Pro focused on print quality, material capability, maintainability, thermal management, wiring, and stability.
overview: I progressively rebuilt a Creality Ender 3 Pro around print quality, expanded material capability, electrical safety, serviceability, and mechanical stability.
objectives: Improve print quality and material compatibility.
Improve safety, cooling, and maintainability.
Reduce alignment and vibration issues.
process: Assembled and calibrated the stock machine.
Replaced the mainboard and extruder, added connectors, and redesigned electronics packaging.
Added bracing, a second Z leadscrew, and a custom alignment mechanism.
results: Completed a substantially upgraded printer with improved maintainability and broader capability.

title: 3D Printed Head-Tracking RC Airplane
summary: A repairable 3D-printed RC aircraft with a planned Arduino head-tracking FPV camera gimbal and modular electronics packaging.
overview: This project explores a repairable 3D-printed RC aircraft with a head-tracking FPV camera. Damaged structural parts can be reprinted instead of replacing a conventional airframe.
objectives: Create a repairable printable airframe.
Minimize mass while maintaining structure.
Implement pilot head-tracking for the camera.
Protect and modularize expensive electronics.
process: Selected one-wall printed construction with internal ribbing.
Designed an Arduino-based head tracker and servo gimbal architecture.
Defined a protected electronics module transferable between airframes.
results: Airframe design remains in progress.
Head-tracking and wiring are documented at the design level.
No completed flight test is claimed yet.
evidence: Validate the aircraft after first flight.

title: Portable Vertical-Axis Wind Turbine
summary: A compact wind-powered backcountry charging system combining a vertical-axis turbine, custom generator work, rectification, and regulated USB output.
overview: This project is a portable wind-powered generator intended for backcountry canoe and camping trips. A vertical-axis architecture was selected for changing wind directions and simple deployment.
objectives: Portable and weather resistant.
Charge a power bank remotely.
Keep rotor/blade mass low.
Develop a compact generator and conversion chain.
process: Modeled rotor, stator, blade mounting, and weatherproofing.
Defined a 3-phase rectifier and buck stage.
Began coil sizing around required voltage/current.
results: Major mechanical structures are designed.
Electrical selection and coil development are ongoing.
No completed output-power test is claimed yet.

title: Machine-Learning Self-Driving Car
summary: A Raspberry Pi camera-based model car trained to follow a curved track using Python and neural-network steering prediction.
overview: This university team project used a Raspberry Pi model car, onboard camera, Python, and machine learning to follow a curved track.
objectives: Build a camera-based track-following car.
Apply ML to a physical robotics platform.
Compare multiple neural-network candidates.
process: Assembled and wired the Raspberry Pi car and camera.
Selected and tested the best network on the physical track.
results: The car successfully followed the path.
Selected model achieved MSE 9.9 and R² 97.03%.
Received a documented grade of 93%.
evidence: Make the model architecture easy to inspect.
Support performance claims if originals remain.

title: Guitar Filter & Compressor
summary: A MATLAB frequency-domain audio project that isolates chord tones and normalizes their amplitudes with band-pass filtering and compression.
overview: This individual project used MATLAB to process an acoustic-guitar chord in the frequency domain, isolate notes, and normalize their amplitudes.
objectives: Apply Fourier/filter concepts to audio.
Equalize tone amplitudes.
Generalize beyond the fixed assignment input.
process: Analyzed the chord in the frequency domain.
Created band-pass filters around target notes.
Modified the code for user-selected audio and chord frequencies.
results: Reduced final tone-amplitude variance to 1.2%.
Received a documented grade of 98%.

Prepare the car for competition.

results: The car competed in Virginia in summer 2022.
